views.name: cards_core_projection
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cards.id AS id,
  cards.name AS name,
  cards.uuid AS uuid,
  cards.cardKingdomFoilId AS cardKingdomFoilId,
  cards.cardKingdomId AS cardKingdomId,
  cards.setCode AS setCode,
  cards.rarity AS rarity
FROM cards

params.description: Provides one-row-per-card basic identifying attributes (id, name, uuid, cardKingdom IDs, set code, rarity).
params.when_to_use: Look up card-level attributes by card id or uuid | Filter or join other data to card identity (e.g., transactions, inventory) using card id/uuid | Build aggregated metrics at the card grain by composing this view as the dimensional/cardinality-preserving source of card attributes | Enrich event-level data with card attributes while preserving card-level uniqueness when aggregated correctly
params.output_schema: id: unique card identifier (cards.id) | name: card display name (cards.name) | uuid: card UUID identifier (cards.uuid) | cardKingdomFoilId: CardKingdom foil SKU/ID for this card (cards.cardKingdomFoilId) | cardKingdomId: CardKingdom non-foil SKU/ID for this card (cards.cardKingdomId) | setCode: code for the set this card belongs to (cards.setCode) | rarity: rarity classification for the card (cards.rarity)
params.grounded_columns: cards.id | cards.name | cards.uuid | cards.cardKingdomFoilId | cards.cardKingdomId | cards.setCode | cards.rarity
params.metric: No derived numeric aggregates are defined by this view. All columns are direct projections from the base table. | If you need a card-count metric: card_count = COUNT(DISTINCT cards.id) when aggregating multiple rows from this view or from joins that preserve card uniqueness.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables that are one-to-one with cards on cards.id (or cards.uuid) — safe because this view is one-row-per-card so its attributes are not duplicated. | Safe: join to a sets/view of sets on setCode = set.code — safe if sets is one-row-per-set (this view remains one-row-per-card). | Safe: join to a CardKingdom lookup on cardKingdomId or cardKingdomFoilId when that lookup is one-row-per-cardKingdomId — does not duplicate rows. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables (for example: transactions, sales_lines, card_images where multiple rows per card may exist) without re-aggregation, because joining a one-row-per-card view to a many-row-per-card table will multiply card-level rows and thus duplicate any measures derived at the card grain. Instead, pre-aggregate the many-side (e.g., SUM(sales.amount) GROUP BY card_id) or perform a DISTINCT/ROW_NUMBER trick to enforce one row per card before joining. | When composing metrics: if you join this view to event-level tables and then compute aggregates, ensure you aggregate on the event table keys (not simply COUNT(*) on the join) or use COUNT(DISTINCT cards.id) to avoid inflated counts. | Primary keys/uniqueness: cards.id (grain) is the unique key for this view. Use cards.id or cards.uuid as join keys to preserve cardinality.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-card basic identifying attributes (id, name, uuid, cardKingdom IDs, set code, rarity).

views.name: cards_with_legalities
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS id,
  c.uuid AS uuid,
  c.name AS name,
  c.setCode AS setCode,
  c.rarity AS rarity,
  l.format AS format,
  l.status AS status,
  c.cardKingdomFoilId AS cardKingdomFoilId,
  c.cardKingdomId AS cardKingdomId
FROM cards_core_projection c
LEFT JOIN legalities l
  ON l.uuid = c.uuid

params.description: Provides card-level rows enriched with format-specific legality status by card UUID and format.
params.when_to_use: Look up a card's legality status for a given format (e.g., "Is card X legal in Modern?"). | List cards along with their set, rarity and Card Kingdom identifiers filtered by format and legality (e.g., "All legal cards in Standard"). | Compose higher-level aggregations (counts, existence checks) of cards by format/status, set, or rarity. | Join card metadata to other card-level facts (prices, inventory) while preserving one-row-per-(id,format) granularity.
params.output_schema: id: primary card id from cards_core_projection.id (cards_core_projection.id) — the local integer PK that identifies the card row | uuid: card UUID from cards_core_projection.uuid (cards_core_projection.uuid) — canonical card identifier used to join to legalities and other UUID-keyed resources | name: card name from cards_core_projection.name (cards_core_projection.name) | setCode: set code from cards_core_projection.setCode (cards_core_projection.setCode) | rarity: rarity string from cards_core_projection.rarity (cards_core_projection.rarity) | format: format identifier from legalities.format (legalities.format) — the format for which the legality/status applies | status: legality status from legalities.status (legalities.status) — the legality value (e.g., legal, banned, restricted) for the given format | cardKingdomFoilId: Card Kingdom foil product id from cards_core_projection.cardKingdomFoilId (cards_core_projection.cardKingdomFoilId) | cardKingdomId: Card Kingdom non-foil product id from cards_core_projection.cardKingdomId (cards_core_projection.cardKingdomId)
params.grounded_columns: cards_core_projection.id | cards_core_projection.uuid | cards_core_projection.name | cards_core_projection.setCode | cards_core_projection.rarity | cards_core_projection.cardKingdomFoilId | cards_core_projection.cardKingdomId | legalities.uuid | legalities.format | legalities.status
params.metric: row_count = count(*) over the view's grain (implicit): one row per (cards_core_projection.id, legalities.format) when a matching legality exists, otherwise one row per cards_core_projection.id with NULLs for legalities columns due to LEFT JOIN | is_legal_flag = CASE WHEN status = 'legal' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END (derivable expression on legalities.status, computed by consumers as needed)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensions that are one-to-one with cards_core_projection at the card id or uuid level — for example, join to a card_details view on cards_core_projection.id or cards_core_projection.uuid — safe because this view is one-row-per (id,format) and these joins will not duplicate rows when the dimension is one-row-per-card. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a sets dimension on setCode (e.g., sets.code = cards_with_legalities.setCode) — safe because sets is one-row-per-setCode, so it will not multiply this view's rows. | do NOT join directly to any table/view that is one-to-many per card (for example: printings, prices_history, inventories, reviews) without first aggregating that one-to-many into one row per (id) or per (id,format) as appropriate. Such joins would duplicate rows and therefore multiply any counts or sums derived from this view. | if you need to bring in measures from one-to-many tables (prices, listings, printings), pre-aggregate those tables to the same grain as this view (either per card id or per (card id, format) if the measure is format-specific) and then join on the matching keys to avoid duplicating this view's rows/measures. | LEFT JOIN semantics note: this view uses a LEFT JOIN from cards_core_projection to legalities on uuid. That means for cards without a matching legalities row the format and status columns will be NULL. If you INNER JOIN this view downstream to a table keyed by (id, format), you may filter out those NULL-legalities rows — ensure the join preserves the intended cardinality. | keys to join on: prefer cards_with_legalities.id = other.card_id or cards_with_legalities.uuid = other.uuid for card-level joins; use cards_with_legalities.format = other.format when the other side is keyed by format as well.

views.name: cards_foreign_translations
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS id,
  c.uuid AS uuid,
  c.name AS name,
  f.language AS language,
  f.name AS foreign_name,
  f.text AS foreign_text,
  c.cardKingdomFoilId AS cardKingdomFoilId,
  c.cardKingdomId AS cardKingdomId
FROM cards_core_projection c
JOIN foreign_data f
  ON f.uuid = c.uuid

params.description: Provides card rows enriched with a single matched foreign-language translation (one row per card UUID + language).
params.when_to_use: Retrieve card metadata together with a specific foreign-language name/text for reporting or display. | Filter or group cards by language-specific fields (foreign_name, foreign_text). | Compose additional aggregations or joins that expect one row per card UUID and language (e.g., counts per language, joins to pricing by card id) while preserving cardinality when done correctly.
params.output_schema: id: primary integer id of the card from cards_core_projection.id | uuid: canonical UUID of the card from cards_core_projection.uuid | name: default (base) card name from cards_core_projection.name | language: language code/identifier for this translation from foreign_data.language | foreign_name: translated name text from foreign_data.name | foreign_text: translated rules/flavor text from foreign_data.text | cardKingdomFoilId: external Card Kingdom foil identifier from cards_core_projection.cardKingdomFoilId | cardKingdomId: external Card Kingdom non-foil identifier from cards_core_projection.cardKingdomId
params.grounded_columns: cards_core_projection.id | cards_core_projection.uuid | cards_core_projection.name | cards_core_projection.cardKingdomFoilId | cards_core_projection.cardKingdomId | foreign_data.uuid | foreign_data.language | foreign_data.name | foreign_data.text
params.metric: row_grain = (id, language)  -- the declared grain: one row per cards_core_projection.id and foreign_data.language (as produced by the JOIN on uuid). | note: there are no aggregate metrics defined in this view; all output columns are direct projections of base columns (no SUM/COUNT/AVG etc.).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_core_projection (NORM) on id OR uuid — safe because this view's rows are derived directly from cards_core_projection (1:1 per id/uuid) and the join will not multiply rows when you join back to the same base on the same key. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a dimensions table that is 1:1 per language (e.g., languages metadata) on language — safe because languages are expected unique per language code so this view's measures are not duplicated. | do NOT blindly join to one-to-many tables (e.g., card_printings, multiple prices per card, or other multi-row child tables keyed only by uuid or id) without first aggregating the child table to the (id, language) or id level. Such joins will multiply rows and thus multiply any measures derived from this view because cards_foreign_translations has one row per (id, language) and a many-side join will create multiple rows per (id, language). | If you must combine with a one-to-many relation (for example, many price records per card), either: (a) aggregate the many-side to the same grain as this view (id OR (id, language) if the many-side is language-scoped) before joining, or (b) perform the join and then re-aggregate the result to the desired grain (id, language) using appropriate aggregates (e.g., SUM, AVG) to avoid double-counting. | When joining to cards_with_legalities (JOIN) ensure the join key and expected cardinality: if cards_with_legalities is one-row-per-card (id or uuid), join on id/uuid is safe; if it is one-to-many (e.g., one row per format), either filter/aggregate legalities to one row per card first or join on both id and format to intentionally broaden the grain. | Because this view sources foreign_data by joining on uuid, it relies on foreign_data having at most one row per (uuid, language) for the declared grain. If foreign_data contains multiple translations per (uuid, language), this view will already reflect that multiplicity; downstream planners should treat the view as potentially multi-row per id if foreign_data is multi-row and must aggregate accordingly.

views.name: cards_core_projection_3
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cards.id AS id,
  cards.name AS name,
  cards.uuid AS uuid,
  cards.borderColor AS borderColor,
  cards.cardKingdomId AS cardKingdomId,
  cards.cardKingdomFoilId AS cardKingdomFoilId,
  cards.availability AS availability,
  cards.setCode AS setCode
FROM cards

params.description: A projection of core card attributes (one row per card id) used to look up identifying and display properties for cards.
params.when_to_use: Fetch basic card metadata by id, name, uuid, or setCode for display, linking, or filtering. | Compose into joins where a single row per card is required (e.g., enrich transactions, inventory, or references with card display fields). | Serve as the canonical card dimension for reporting when no aggregation of card-level many-side data is needed.
params.output_schema: id: the primary identifier for the card, derived from cards.id | name: the human-readable name of the card, derived from cards.name | uuid: the globally unique identifier of the card, derived from cards.uuid | borderColor: the card's border color attribute used for display, derived from cards.borderColor | cardKingdomId: numeric/string id for CardKingdom storefront mapping, derived from cards.cardKingdomId | cardKingdomFoilId: numeric/string id for CardKingdom foil mapping, derived from cards.cardKingdomFoilId | availability: availability status/code for the card, derived from cards.availability | setCode: set identifier/code that the card belongs to, derived from cards.setCode
params.grounded_columns: cards.id | cards.name | cards.uuid | cards.borderColor | cards.cardKingdomId | cards.cardKingdomFoilId | cards.availability | cards.setCode
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are produced by this projection. All outputs are direct column projections from the cards table (identity mappings). Example: id = cards.id (no aggregation).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any fact or dimension on cards.id (or cards.uuid if present) using a many-to-one or many-to-many -> one relationship where the cards table is the one side (e.g., inventory.card_id -> cards.id, sales.card_id -> cards.id) — safe because this view is one-row-per-card id so its columns will not be duplicated by the join. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sibling card dimension views that are also one-row-per-card (for example cards_core_projection or other normalized card projections) on id or uuid — safe because keys are one-to-one. | Do NOT join this view directly to known one-to-many children of cards (for example a hypothetical cards_images, cards_prices_history, cards_legalities with multiple rows per card) without first aggregating or selecting a single child row per card, because such joins will multiply the card rows and thus duplicate card-level attributes and any metrics derived from counts of rows. If you need child information, either: | - aggregate the child table to one row per card (e.g., latest_price(card_id) or count_pricerecords(card_id)), then join aggregated result to this view on id; OR | - join this view as the driving table and ensure downstream queries apply GROUP BY cards_core_projection_3.id and appropriate aggregations to avoid duplication. | When composing into analytical models: because this view contains no numeric measures/aggregates, duplication will primarily affect counts or sums derived after joining. Treat this view as a dimension (card-level attributes); protect metrics by performing aggregations on the fact side before joining or by using DISTINCT/GROUP BY on card id as appropriate.

views.name: cards_with_legalities_4
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cards.id AS id,
  cards.uuid AS uuid,
  cards.name AS name,
  cards.setCode AS setCode,
  cards.borderColor AS borderColor,
  cards.cardKingdomId AS cardKingdomId,
  cards.cardKingdomFoilId AS cardKingdomFoilId,
  cards.availability AS availability,
  legalities.format AS format,
  legalities.status AS status
FROM cards
JOIN legalities ON legalities.uuid = cards.uuid

params.description: Provides one row per card-legalities pairing (grain: cards.id + legalities.id), answering which legal formats and statuses apply to each card together with core card identifiers and storefront IDs.
params.when_to_use: List all legal formats and their status for each card (e.g., show which formats a specific card is legal/illegal/banned/restricted). | Filter cards by a specific format/status and return card identifiers and storefront IDs for downstream lookups. | Compose into dashboards or further SQL that needs card metadata (id, uuid, name, setCode) alongside the legalities row (format, status). | Join to pricing/marketplace tables keyed by cardKingdomId or cardKingdomFoilId to display prices for cards that are legal in a given format (but follow cardinality guidance below).
params.output_schema: id: cards.id — internal numeric primary key for the card (from cards.id). | uuid: cards.uuid — globally unique identifier for the card (from cards.uuid); used to join card-level entities that reference uuid. | name: cards.name — human-readable card name (from cards.name). | setCode: cards.setCode — the set code this card printing belongs to (from cards.setCode). | borderColor: cards.borderColor — card border color attribute (from cards.borderColor). | cardKingdomId: cards.cardKingdomId — marketplace/storefront identifier (Card Kingdom non-foil) (from cards.cardKingdomId). | cardKingdomFoilId: cards.cardKingdomFoilId — marketplace/storefront identifier (Card Kingdom foil) (from cards.cardKingdomFoilId). | availability: cards.availability — card availability descriptor (from cards.availability). | format: legalities.format — name of the constructed format or play format (from legalities.format). | status: legalities.status — legality status in that format (e.g., legal, banned, restricted) (from legalities.status).
params.grounded_columns: cards.id | cards.uuid | cards.name | cards.setCode | cards.borderColor | cards.cardKingdomId | cards.cardKingdomFoilId | cards.availability | legalities.id | legalities.uuid | legalities.format | legalities.status
params.metric: There are no aggregated metrics in this view; all outputs are direct column projections. If you need counts you must aggregate explicitly on top of this view. Example derived metric definitions you can compute from this view: | card_row_count = COUNT(*) grouped by nothing — counts card × legality rows (i.e., number of (card,format) pairs returned). | cards_per_format(format) = COUNT(DISTINCT id) FILTER (WHERE format = <format_name>) — counts distinct cards that have a row for a specific format. | legal_cards_per_format(format) = COUNT(DISTINCT id) FILTER (WHERE format = <format_name> AND status = 'legal').
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: | Safe to join (one-to-one or many-to-one into this view) without duplicating measures: |  - Join to dimension tables keyed by cards.id or cards.uuid (for example, a single-row card_details view keyed by cards.id or cards.uuid) — safe because for each row in this view there is at most one matching row in the dimension, so measures aggregated from this view are not multiplied. |  - Join to single-row lookup tables keyed by legalities.id (if such an entity exists) — safe because legalities.id is unique per legal row in the base legalities table. | Unsafe to join (one-to-many) without re-aggregation or de-duplication: |  - Do NOT freely join to tables that have many rows per card (e.g., translations table, prices history table, printings table that has multiple printings per cards.id, or a marketplace_prices table with multiple price records per cardKingdomId) unless you first aggregate the many-side to one row per cards.id or per legalities.id. Joining such one-to-many tables will multiply this view's rows and any counts/sums derived from it. |  - Example unsafe join: joining cards_with_legalities_4 to a translations table (cards_foreign_translations) on cards.id without deduplicating translations will replicate the same (card,format) row for every translation row, inflating counts. | Recommended composition patterns: |  - If you need price or time-series data per card, aggregate the price table to one row per card (e.g., latest_price per cardKingdomId) and then join to this view on cardKingdomId/cardKingdomFoilId to avoid row multiplication. |  - If you need to combine legalities with other card-level projections (cards_core_projection or cards_core_projection_3), join on cards.id or cards.uuid — those are card-level one-to-one/one-row-per-card projections, so they won't duplicate rows beyond this view's grain. |  - To compute metrics like number of legal cards per format, aggregate this view by format and status (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT id) or COUNT(*) depending on desired cardinality) rather than joining to additional many-side tables before aggregation.

views.description: Provides one row per card-legalities pairing (grain: cards.id + legalities.id), answering which legal formats and statuses apply to each card together with core card identifiers and storefront IDs.

views.name: cards_with_foreign_translations
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cards.id AS id,
  cards.uuid AS uuid,
  cards.name AS name,
  cards.setCode AS setCode,
  cards.borderColor AS borderColor,
  cards.cardKingdomId AS cardKingdomId,
  cards.cardKingdomFoilId AS cardKingdomFoilId,
  cards.availability AS availability,
  foreign_data.language AS "foreign_data.language",
  foreign_data.name AS "foreign_data.name",
  foreign_data.text AS "foreign_data.text"
FROM cards
JOIN foreign_data ON foreign_data.uuid = cards.uuid

params.description: Provides card-level rows enriched with one or more foreign-language translations (one row per combination of cards.id and foreign_data.id), useful for inspecting card metadata alongside its foreign-language name and text.
params.when_to_use: Show card metadata together with a specific foreign-language translation (e.g., display a card and its Japanese name/text). | Filter or aggregate cards by translation language (e.g., count cards that have a Spanish translation). | Compose further joins or filters that preserve the one-row-per-(cards.id, foreign_data.id) grain (for example, join to sets or printings when those are 1:1 to cards or to aggregations keyed to card id).
params.output_schema: id: the internal surrogate primary key of the card from cards.id | uuid: the card's UUID from cards.uuid (used to correlate card records across tables) | name: the canonical (default) card name from cards.name | setCode: the set code the card belongs to from cards.setCode | borderColor: the border color attribute of the card from cards.borderColor | cardKingdomId: CardKingdom product id (non-foil) from cards.cardKingdomId | cardKingdomFoilId: CardKingdom product id (foil) from cards.cardKingdomFoilId | availability: availability metadata for the card from cards.availability | foreign_data.language: language code of the translation from foreign_data.language | foreign_data.name: translated name text from foreign_data.name | foreign_data.text: translated card text from foreign_data.text
params.grounded_columns: cards.id | cards.uuid | cards.name | cards.setCode | cards.borderColor | cards.cardKingdomId | cards.cardKingdomFoilId | cards.availability | foreign_data.id | foreign_data.uuid | foreign_data.language | foreign_data.name | foreign_data.text
params.metric: row_grain = combination(cards.id, foreign_data.id) -- this view is at the (cards.id, foreign_data.id) grain | no_aggregates = this view exposes base columns only; no derived numeric aggregates are defined here
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a card-level (one-row-per-cards.id) dimension/view on cards.id — safe because cards_with_foreign_translations already has one row per (cards.id, foreign_data.id) and joining a 1:1 card dimension will not duplicate rows. Example: join to cards_core_projection ON cards_core_projection.id = cards_with_foreign_translations.id. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a UUID-keyed table/view on uuid (one-row-per-uuid) — safe for the same reason. Example: join to any view keyed by cards.uuid on uuid. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT join directly to a one-to-many table/view keyed to cards.id (for example a printings table or legalities view that has multiple rows per card) without first aggregating that table to one row per cards.id or otherwise de-duplicating, because doing so will multiply rows and thus multiply any counts or row-level measures derived from this view. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT join another translation table that is also many-per-card (e.g., another foreign_data alias) without deduplicating, because it will create a cross-product between translations and inflate counts. | safe-composition pattern: if you need measures from a 1-to-many child (for example, number_of_printings), pre-aggregate the child to one row per cards.id (e.g., SELECT card_id, COUNT(*) AS printing_count FROM printings GROUP BY card_id) then join that aggregation to this view on cards.id to avoid duplicating translation rows. | when aggregating downstream: if you aggregate over cards_with_foreign_translations and intend metrics per card (not per translation), group by cards.id (or use COUNT(DISTINCT cards.id)) to avoid counting translations as separate cards.

views.description: Provides card-level rows enriched with one or more foreign-language translations (one row per combination of cards.id and foreign_data.id), useful for inspecting card metadata alongside its foreign-language name and text.

views.name: cards_core_attributes
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  name,
  setCode,
  number,
  rarity,
  manaCost,
  types,
  subtypes,
  colors,
  colorIdentity,
  originalReleaseDate AS releasedate,
  printings
FROM cards

params.description: Provides one-row-per-card core descriptive attributes (identity, print/edition metadata, and gameplay characteristics).
params.when_to_use: Fetch core card details by id, uuid, name, or setCode (e.g., show card page or list of cards). | Build higher-level aggregates or joins that treat each card as a single entity (e.g., count cards by rarity, group by color). | Compose with other views that add one-row-per-card facts (legalities, projections) without changing cardinality.
params.output_schema: id: internal primary identifier for the card — sourced from cards.id | uuid: global unique identifier for the card — sourced from cards.uuid | name: printed card name/title — sourced from cards.name | setCode: code of the set/edition this card printing belongs to — sourced from cards.setCode | number: collector number of the card within its set/printing — sourced from cards.number | rarity: rarity classification of this card printing (e.g., common/uncommon/rare) — sourced from cards.rarity | manaCost: mana cost string for the card (as stored) — sourced from cards.manaCost | types: card type line (e.g., Creature, Instant) — sourced from cards.types | subtypes: card subtype line (e.g., Elf, Warrior) — sourced from cards.subtypes | colors: list/representation of card colors — sourced from cards.colors | colorIdentity: color identity used for deck-building rules — sourced from cards.colorIdentity | releasedate: original release date of the card (renamed from originalReleaseDate) — sourced from cards.originalReleaseDate | printings: representation/list of printings for this card (as stored) — sourced from cards.printings
params.grounded_columns: cards.id | cards.uuid | cards.name | cards.setCode | cards.number | cards.rarity | cards.manaCost | cards.types | cards.subtypes | cards.colors | cards.colorIdentity | cards.originalReleaseDate | cards.printings
params.metric: id = cards.id | uuid = cards.uuid | name = cards.name | setCode = cards.setCode | number = cards.number | rarity = cards.rarity | manaCost = cards.manaCost | types = cards.types | subtypes = cards.subtypes | colors = cards.colors | colorIdentity = cards.colorIdentity | releasedate = cards.originalReleaseDate | printings = cards.printings
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_with_legalities (or cards_with_legalities_4) on cards_core_attributes.id = cards_with_legalities.card_id — safe because legalities views are defined as one-row-per-card (they augment the same card grain) so joining preserves one row per card and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to cards_core_projection or cards_core_projection_3 on id (cards_core_attributes.id = cards_core_projection.id) — safe because these sibling projection views share the same grain (one row per card id). | cardinality-UNSAFE guidance: do NOT blindly join to one-to-many tables/views such as cards_foreign_translations or cards_with_foreign_translations without aggregation first — these are multi-row per card (translations/foreign printings) and would duplicate this view's rows/measures. If you need translation fields, aggregate translations (e.g., array_agg or string_agg grouped by cards_core_attributes.id) first, then join the aggregated result back on id. | cardinality-UNSAFE guidance: when joining to any table that contains multiple printings, editions, or other repeated rows per card id, either (a) restrict to a single row per card (e.g., by filtering to canonical printing) or (b) pre-aggregate counts/lists by card id before joining to avoid multiplying rows. | note on joins using setCode/uuid/number: you may join on (id) when combining per-card attributes. Joins on setCode or uuid are acceptable if the target view/table is one-row-per-(setCode or uuid) respectively; verify the sibling view grain before joining to ensure join preserves cardinality.

views.name: card_legalities_by_format
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  uuid,
  format,
  status

views.name: cards_power_status_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS id,
  c.uuid AS uuid,
  c.power AS power,
  CASE
    WHEN c.power IS NULL THEN 1
    WHEN trim(c.power) = '' THEN 1
    WHEN lower(trim(c.power)) IN ('?', 'unknown', '*', '—', '—') THEN 1

Same row-scope as id; useful for cross-system joins. | power: the raw power text string for the card (from cards.power). This is the base textual value as stored in the cards table. | power_is_unknown: binary flag (0/1) computed from cards.power indicating whether the power should be considered unknown/missing. Derived by a CASE expression that treats NULL, empty/whitespace, explicit tokens like '?', 'unknown', '*', '—' and any string containing '*' or '?' as unknown (1), otherwise 0.

  c.id AS id,
  -- determine powerless: true if power is NULL or empty string or equal to "*unknown*" marker;
